tagline: Along the Old Valley Pike, with side roads into the mountains.
intro: The Old Valley Pike, US 11, runs through the Shenandoah Valley from Strasburg, settled by German-speaking Pennsylvanians and later nicknamed Pot Town for its earthenware, through Woodstock and Edinburg to New Market. The side roads head for the mountains. One crosses Edinburg Gap toward Camp Roosevelt in the Fort Valley, and another climbs Orkney Grade, through a narrow valley under Great North Mountain, to Orkney Springs.
At the south end of the pike, VMI cadets joined the Confederate charge at New Market in May 1864. Every year cadets still commemorate their 85-mile march from Lexington.

moments.title: Edinburg Mill
moments.text: Sheridan's troops set this Stony Creek mill afire, local women talked them into saving the flour, the fire was put out, and the mill kept grinding until 1978.

moments.title: Fort Valley
moments.text: The valley within the valley, 23 miles long between the Massanutten ridges and almost entirely closed in, with Passage Creek running down the middle of it.

moments.title: Orkney Springs
moments.text: Its spring hotels were consolidated into the Orkney Springs Hotel, whose Virginia House of the 1870s is believed to be the largest wooden building in Virginia.
